channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Trump on Iran: 'Humanitarian crisis of epic proportions'
item.description:
US President Donald Trump addressed the economic situation in Iran amid increasing US sanctions and condemned the regime for executing protesters.
"The failing Islamic Republic of Iran is not paying large segments of their military, while at the same time killing protesters, even when they are not protesting, at levels not seen before. It is a humanitarian crisis of epic proportions, and must be stopped," he wrote on Truth Social.

item.title: ‘Trump is rewarding Hamas': Nadia Matar calls to halt Gaza aid, reconstruction
item.description: Sovereignty Movement co-chair speaks to Arutz Sheva at demonstration outside ISF base, calls to cancel agreement and restore Israeli sovereignty and Jewish settlement in Gaza.

item.title: Smotrich backs Sukkot memorial demolition, with one major caveat
item.description: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said the terror memorial should have been removed long ago, but insisted that only the IDF has the authority to carry out such actions.

item.title: 'A clear warning' | Watch: IDF strikes Hamas weapons sites in mosques
item.description: IDF launches series of strikes targeting five Hamas weapon storage facilities and a launch site inside mosques and alongside humanitarian infrastructure in the Gaza Strip.

item.title: Arab recruitment to Israel Police plummets
item.description: Official figures show a sharp decline in Arab recruitment to the Israel Police, as ministry officials point to stricter vetting and Hebrew requirements.

item.title: Netanyahu condemns Sukkot: 'Prevents the IDF from focusing on its missions'
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticized MK Tzvi Sukkot for entering Arab villages in Samaria to destroy monuments to terrorists, saying the MK took the law into his own hands.
“The IDF is the sovereign authority in Judea and Samaria and is responsible for implementing the decisions of the political echelon. Taking the law into one’s own hands, particularly by public officials, is unacceptable and prevents the IDF from focusing on its missions against terrorism and incitement," Netanyahu stated.

item.title: Smotrich reprimands Sukkot, instructs him not to repeat his actions
item.description:
Religious Zionist Party chairman Bezalel Smotrich reprimanded MK Tzvi Sukkot for entering Palestinian Arab villages to destroy monuments to terrorists.
Smotrich told Sukkot that the proper course is to act with authorization and within the bounds of one’s authority, “as is done on matters concerning Judea and Samaria communities," and demanded that he not do anything like this again.

item.title: Pro-Palestinian activists target Israeli soccer player
item.description: Hours before Manor Solomon was set to face fellow Israeli Daniel Peretz, pro-Palestinian activists protested outside West Ham's training ground and demanded the club release the Israeli star.

item.title: IDF responds to Sukkot: 'Plans had been drawn up to demolish the monument'
item.description: IDF officials clarified on Tuesday morning that plans had been drawn up to demolish the monument smashed by MK Sukkot in the village of Madama, near Yitzhar, and that the operation was scheduled to take place in the coming weeks. “Dozens of similar monuments have already been demolished in Judea and Samaria, and an operation to demolish this monument legally and in an orderly manner by the security forces was scheduled to take place in the coming weeks. Preliminary inspections were also conducted by the Samaria Brigade ahead of the demolition of monuments," the officials said.

item.title: Sa'ar against Sukkot: Decisions in Judea and Samaria must be made by state and IDF
item.description:
Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar criticized MK Zvi Sukkot, stressing that decisions in Judea and Samaria must be made and implemented solely by the state, the IDF, and the security forces.
“This is also the message that elected officials should convey to the public. Unfortunately, MK Sukkot knowingly did the opposite," he said.

item.title: MK Tal on Tzvi Sukkot: 'Have we simply decided to commit political suicide?'
item.description: MK Ohad Tal criticized fellow Religious Zionist Party MK Tzvi Sukkot for entering Arab villages to destroy monuments to terrorists. In internal Religious Zionist Party groups, he wrote: “I want to understand - was this move coordinated with the campaign? Is there some deep strategy behind it that I am completely missing, or have we simply decided to commit political suicide once and for all? I’m genuinely asking."

item.title: IDF and police evacuate Kafr Aqab UNRWA compound
item.description: IDF, Israel Police, and Jerusalem Municipality began evacuating the UNRWA in Kafr Aqab.

item.title: ‘We will stop it’: Gaza border residents protest outside international force base
item.description: Gaza envelope residents block aid trucks outside the international force base at Kerem Shalom, warning against rebuilding Gaza before Hamas is disarmed.

item.title: U.S. threatens sanctions on firms still doing business with Iran
item.description: Washington is moving to isolate Iran from the global economy, threatening sanctions against entities that continue trading with Tehran.

item.title: T’shuva makes the world go ‘round
item.description: While Rabbi Kook emphasizes that the teshuva of the Jewish People and a return to the Torah go hand-in-hand, he indicates that a preliminary stage of national revival will bring this spiritual awakening to pass.

item.title: The great mission of Torah teachers
item.description: The study of Torah, through which the spiritual world is sustained, is carried out by Torah scholars and by all Jews who set aside regular times for Torah study.

item.title: MK takes matters into his own hands, smashes terrorist monuments
item.description: MK Tzvi Sukkot takes a sledgehammer to monuments honoring terrorists near Yitzhar, saying authorities failed to act despite his earlier demands.

item.title: Yeshiva student arrested in late-night military raid
item.description: Military Police officers in civilian clothes raided a family home in Haifa late at night and arrested a 22-year-old yeshiva graduate.

item.title: Mossad chief backs controversial Bedouin industrial zone
item.description: Mossad Director Roman Gofman has thrown his support behind a disputed plan for a 200-dunam industrial zone near Bir Hadaj, arguing that jobs could strengthen security and weaken criminal elements.

item.title: Antisemites can treat Zionists with compassion
item.description: After Oct 7 the government of South Africa lost no time dragging Israel to The Hague for genocide in Gaza. It also got bosom buddy Hamas which had dragged slain IDF Capt Daniel Perez to Gaza, to return his mortal remains to the mother and father, who happens to be President of the World Zionist Organisation.

item.title: Mystery men spotted emerging from NYC sewer
item.description: Three people wearing coveralls and headlamps were caught on video climbing out of a Manhattan sewer at 4 a.m., raising fresh questions about a string of mysterious underground incidents across New York City.

item.title: Pakistan says ‘significant progress’ made in talks with Iranian leaders
item.description: Pakistan says ‘significant progress’ was made in Tehran talks on the Iran-US conflict, regional tensions, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and a settlement.

item.title: Why is Mark Ruffalo using the genocide libel again?
item.description: Mark Ruffalo once admitted the “Genocide" libel fuels antisemitism. Now he’s doing it again? Opinion.

item.title: Destroying the Evidence: UNESCO against its own nature
item.description: What happens when the custodian of memory alters it? Archaeology does not change its nature according to who operates the excavator.

item.title: Syria sentences Assad-era grand mufti to life in prison
item.description: A Syrian court sentences former grand mufti Ahmed Hassoun to life in prison after convicting him of inciting civil war and intentional killing.

item.title: Netherlands pulls out of 2027 Eurovision over Israel and Gaza war
item.description: The Netherlands will skip Eurovision 2027, claiming the Gaza war and Israel's participation have undermined the contest's political neutrality.

item.title: 'Disgraceful and shameful' | MK Sukkot demands arrest of PA police officers
item.description: MK Tzvi Sukkot visits scene where an Israeli reservist was attacked by PA police officers, calls on defense establishment to bring those involved to justice.

item.title: US offers up to $10 million for information on five senior IRGC commanders
item.description: US State Department is offering up to $10 million and possible relocation for information on five senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commanders.

item.title: Erdan on Gaza border: Explosive kites are back - time to make Hamas pay a heavy price
item.description: Unity Party chairman Gilad Erdan and Col. (res.) Hezi Nechama tour the Gaza border area following the renewed launch of explosive kites, call for a change in policy.

item.description: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed distances his campaign from Hasan Piker after the streamer’s remarks about Jewish Americans spark renewed controversy.
